findings.title: Hardcoded API Keys and Secrets in .env Files
findings.description: Multiple sensitive credentials are hardcoded in .env files that are tracked by git or exist in production. The .gitignore does properly exclude .env files, but the damage is already done as secrets may have been committed historically.
findings.impact: Full compromise of cloud services (Aliyun OSS, Doubao TTS, Supabase). Potential unauthorized access to user data stored in Supabase.
recommendation: 1. IMMEDIATELY rotate all exposed secrets
2. Use a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault)
3. Implement .env.production in production deployments only via CI/CD
4. Set up secret rotation policies

findings.title: Wildcard CORS Allow-All Policy
findings.description: Socket.io is configured with origin: '*' which allows connections from any domain. This enables Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH) attacks.
findings.impact: Any malicious website can establish WebSocket connections to the server, potentially: (1) Stealing user sessions, (2) Injecting fake messages, (3) Accessing paired bot data, (4) Performing actions on behalf of authenticated users.
recommendation: 1. Replace origin: '*' with explicit whitelist of allowed origins
2. Example: origin: ['https://trix-3d.com', 'https://your-domain.com']
3. Use origin validation with fallback for development: origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['http://localhost:5173']
4. Consider using origin check with credentials: origin: (origin, callback) => { if (allowedOrigins.includes(origin)) callback(null, true); else callback(new Error('Not allowed')); }

findings.title: Missing Socket.io Authentication
findings.description: Socket.io connections have no authentication or authorization. Any client can connect and perform sensitive operations like pairing, sending messages, or accessing study rooms without proving identity.

socket_events: bot_request_pairing - allows any device to initiate pairing
app_register - accepts any userId without verification

findings.impact: Unauthorized users can: (1) Hijack bot pairing sessions, (2) Send messages as any user, (3) Access/modify study rooms they don't belong to, (4) Unpair other users' bots.
recommendation: 1. Implement JWT authentication for Socket.io connections
2. Use socket.io middleware for auth: io.use((socket, next) => { /* validate JWT */ next(); })
3. Add userId validation against authenticated token
4. Implement room-level authorization (check user belongs to room before allowing actions)

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Socket.io Events
findings.description: While HTTP endpoints have rate limiting (apiLimiter, uploadLimiter, ttsLimiter), Socket.io events have no rate limiting protection.
findings.impact: Vulnerable to: (1) Message flooding attacks, (2) WebSocket connection exhaustion, (3) Bot command abuse, (4) Database resource exhaustion.
recommendation: 1. Implement Socket.io rate limiting using 'socket.io-rate-limiter' or custom middleware
2. Limit events per user per time window
3. Implement connection limits per IP
4. Add per-event type rate limits

findings.title: Webhook Secret Check May Fail Silently
findings.description: The webhook endpoint checks for CLAWBOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET but if this env var is not set, the comparison will still work (undefined !== undefined is false).
findings.impact: If CLAWBOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set, the webhook becomes publicly accessible.
recommendation: 1. Add explicit check: if (!process.env.CLAWBOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET) return res.status(500).json({error: 'Webhook not configured'});
2. Ensure webhook secret is required in server startup validation
3. Use constant-time comparison: crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(authHeader), Buffer.from(process.env.CLAWBOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET))

findings.title: OSS Signed URL Generation Without Authorization
findings.description: The /oss/signed-url endpoint generates signed URLs for any key without verifying the requester's authorization.

evidence.code: app.get('/oss/signed-url', async (req, res) => { const { key } = req.query; ... })

findings.impact: Users can potentially access files belonging to other users by guessing object keys.
recommendation: 1. Add user authentication check before generating signed URLs
2. Validate that the requested key belongs to the requesting user
3. Use path validation to prevent directory traversal

top_3_vulnerabilities.action_required: Rotate all exposed credentials immediately. Move secrets to a secure secrets manager.
